title: GPU tenancy strategy and noise-control: quota enforcement, headroom, and eviction policies
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Goal: Define and implement GPU fleet partitioning and isolation controls for Dedicated customers to ensure throughput guarantees while preventing noisy-neighbor degradation. This ticket captures the end-to-end design, implementation plan, and rollout strategy for tenant separation, quota enforcement, and eviction/headroom policies.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Each dedicated tenant can reserve fraction(s) of GPUs or MIG partitions with enforceable soft and hard quota limits.
2) Noisy-tenant incidents (latency/cold-start spikes, higher token p95) can be mitigated automatically by throttling or migrating work to reserved headroom capacity.
3) Autoscaler honors tenant-level policies (min/max pools, scale targets) and will not starve critical tenants during cluster-wide load.
4) Metrics for per-tenant GPU utilization, preemption events, and throttled requests are exported to Console dashboards.
5) System passes synthetic isolation tests (injection of adversarial load) and integration tests with Dedicated billing and quota metering.
design_decisions:
- Use node-level and GPU-level isolation: prefer MIG for per-tenant hardware isolation where supported; fall back to cgroup/driver-level accounting on mixed fleets.
- Implement two-tier quotas: soft quota (latency-based throttling + queued allowance) and hard quota (reject/evict excess requests).
- Reserve a configurable headroom pool per AZ for emergency overflow to satisfy SLOs for high-priority tenants.
- Eviction policy: prefer preempting best-effort / burst workloads first; do not evict guaranteed-critical traffic without explicit escalation.
- Autoscaler integration: the cluster autoscaler will consider 'tenant min capacity' annotations and a tenant-aware scoring function when choosing when/where to scale up.
- Telemetry: add per-tenant GPU-memory, GPU-utilization, launch latency, and token throughput metrics to enable billing reconciliation and anomaly detection.
implementation_plan:
1) Spec API: Extend Dedicated config schema to accept 'tenancy' blocks (reserved_gpus, use_mig, priority, soft_quota, hard_quota). (Owner: @Ethan)
2) Scheduler changes: tenant-aware binpacking + affinity/anti-affinity rules; support MIG labels in node discovery. (Owner: @Priya)
3) Runtime enforcement: implement cgroup + NVIDIA MIG-aware enforcement agents to throttle or mark processes for eviction. (Owner: @Marco)
4) Autoscaler hook: add per-tenant min/max constraints and a vacancy headroom target. (Owner: @Lena)
5) Metering & billing: extend usage collector to attribute GPU minutes to tenant reservations and to record throttled tokens. (Owner: @Ravi)
6) E2E tests + chaos: build adversarial load generator and run isolation validation in staging. (Owner: @QA Team)
7) Rollout: Canary to non-production tenants -> opt-in pilot with two customers -> global rollout with migration tools.
Links: Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/dedicated/tenancy-policy, PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1345
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for quota accounting and eviction decisions.
- Integration tests between scheduler and runtime enforcement (MIG and non-MIG nodes).
- Load tests: ramp adversarial tenant load to 200% of a node to validate throttling and headroom migration.
- Chaos: kill worker pods mid-launch to validate autoscaler reallocation.
- Performance regression: ensure tail latency for reserved tenants remains within SLO (p95 < configured target).
rollout_notes:
Phase 1 (canary): apply tenancy configs to 3 non-production clusters; monitor isolation metrics for 2 weeks.
Phase 2 (pilot): enable for 2 enterprise customers with strict SLAs; run close monitoring and support on-call.
Phase 3: opt-in for all Reserved customers with migration tooling and a 30-day opt-in window.
Fallback: if eviction policy causes SLA regressions, revert to soft-quota-only mode and open incident runbook.
metrics_and_dashboards:
- Dashboard: Per-tenant GPU utilization, queued requests, throttled request rate, preemption count.
- Alert: tenant throttling > 5% sustained for 5m OR preemptions > 3 in 1h -> P1 pager.
- Billing report: billed GPU-minutes vs reserved GPU-minutes, anomalous overages flagged for review.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Risk: MIG not uniformly available across cloud instance types -> Mitigation: support hybrid strategy with MIG where possible and software isolation elsewhere.
- Risk: Preemption could cause visible failures for some workloads -> Mitigation: default to best-effort eviction only, require customer opt-in for preemptible reservations.
- Risk: Complex scheduler heuristics might increase scheduling latency -> Mitigation: keep scoring function simple, benchmark, and add caches for common tenant placement decisions.
open_questions: Should reserved headroom be shared across tenants in an AZ or partitioned per-tenant?
What default soft_quota/hard_quota ratios make sense for bursty workloads (e.g., 1.5x burst allowance)?
Do we need a per-tenant cost-center label propagated to billing early in the rollout?
